top_stories.title: Rising global costs threaten Mexico’s production costs and food stability | Inflation | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: Rising global costs of fuel and fertilizer, driven by shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, are forcing **Mexican** consumers to tighten budgets and cut back on consumption.  The price hikes for staples like tomatoes, potatoes, beef, and chillies have led to increased consumer spending on food and a drop in sales at local markets.  **Elites**, including **Elvira Pasillas**, professor at the Western Institute of Technology and Higher Education (ITESO), are concerned about the impact this will have on low-income households who spend nearly 70 percent of their earnings on food. The rising cost of fuel, roadblocks, and extortion by organized criminal groups are also contributing to higher prices for meat, produce, and other goods.  The Mexican government has implemented a voluntary agreement with retailers to reduce the fuel tax but this is expected to strain public finances.

top_stories.title: Iran hosts Pakistani delegation amid diplomatic flurry to avert new US strikes | Iran | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf**, **Iran’s parliamentary speaker**, stated that Iran will not compromise on its national rights during a meeting with **Syed Asim Munir**, the Pakistani army chief, in Tehran.  Amidst reports of renewed US strikes on Iran, **Pakistan** has been mediating talks between the two countries. **Marco Rubio**, the US secretary of state, expressed cautious optimism for negotiations while **Trump** is reportedly reviewing options for restarting a bombing campaign. The ceasefire between the US, Israel and Iran, which began in early April, remains largely unchanged despite efforts to extend it.

top_stories.title: Saad Edhi arrives in Karachi after release from illegal Israeli detention - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Saad Edhi**, a Pakistani humanitarian worker, arrived in Karachi on Saturday after being deported from Israel to Turkey.  He was detained by **Israeli forces** during the interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla earlier this week.  The **Foreign Office (FO)** condemned Israel's unlawful interception and expressed Pakistan's support for the Palestinian people.  **Ishaq Dar**, Pakistan's Foreign Minister, thanked Turkey for facilitating Edhi's safe passage to Istanbul.  Edhi had been part of a humanitarian aid mission to Gaza, which was intercepted by **Israeli forces**.

top_stories.title: One more Trinamool councillor from Bidhannagar arrested - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **TMC** councillors from the municipality of Bidhannagar, **West Bengal**, have been arrested in recent days for charges including intimidation, violence, extortion, and money laundering.  The arrests follow a crackdown by the new **BJP** government after the 2021 Assembly election. Several other TMC leaders, including a local union leader and a former minister, have also been arrested on various charges. The arrests come amid allegations of post-poll violence and threats against citizens.

top_stories.title: 'Encouraging progress' made during CDF Munir's Tehran visit: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Field Marshal Asim Munir**, Chief of the Army Staff, concluded intensive negotiations with **Iranian** leadership over the past 24 hours resulting in “encouraging progress towards a final understanding”. The engagements were held in a positive and constructive environment and contributed meaningfully to ongoing mediation efforts aimed at de-escalation and peace.  The discussions focused on expediting the consultative process to support peace and stability in the region, with both sides appreciating Pakistan's role in facilitating dialogue. **US Secretary of State Marco Rubio** praised Pakistan as Washington’s “primary interlocutor” in the talks, highlighting the evolving process resembling a phased stabilization effort rather than comprehensive settlement negotiations.

top_stories.title: Indian-origin cancer specialist banned from practising in UK says, 'I will never work in that country again' - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Shamir Chandran**, an Indian-origin oncologist, has been struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal ruled that his criminal conviction made him a risk to the public.  The **Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS)** found Chandran guilty of controlling and coercive behaviour and cruelty to a person under 16, and he fled the UK before the proceedings. The tribunal deemed allowing Chandran to continue practicing medicine would damage public trust in the profession.

top_stories.title: Five police officers, 13 year-old boy killed in Israeli attack on Gaza | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Israeli** forces attacked a police post in northern Gaza, killing at least five police officers and a 13-year-old boy. **Al Jazeera** reported that the attack came as Israel continues its attacks across the Gaza Strip despite a ceasefire agreement. The **Gaza police directorate** stated that two missiles hit the police post, highlighting a pattern of targeting police and security personnel by **Israel**.  The attacks threaten aid distribution in Gaza while exacerbating a humanitarian crisis.

top_stories.title: World Cup 2026: DR Congo squad told to isolate before entering US - BBC Sport
top_stories.rephrased_article: **DR Congo's** World Cup squad have been instructed to isolate for 21 days in Belgium before entering the United States due to an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. **The White House Task Force for the World Cup** has emphasized that this isolation is crucial to prevent any potential spread of the virus, as entry restrictions imposed by the **Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)** prohibit travel from individuals who have been in affected countries within the past 21 days. The team's training camp was canceled, but they will play friendlies against Denmark and Chile before their World Cup opener against Portugal on June 17th.

top_stories.title: White House pauses removal of detainees to the DRC as Ebola outbreak widens | Ebola | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Trump administration** has temporarily paused the removal of refugees to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) due to a spiraling Ebola outbreak.  Experts argue that this move will not help prevent the spread of the disease, and some fear it could violate international law by sending people back to countries where they may be persecuted. The **US Department of Homeland Security** maintains that it follows health and safety guidelines when conducting removals but did not respond to questions about Zapata's case or future plans for third-country removals during the outbreak.  The **Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)** has implemented screening measures at airports to limit risk, while experts emphasize that travelers from affected areas are unlikely to bring Ebola into the United States.

top_stories.title: DR Congo will not change World Cup preparations despite US Ebola warning | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)** has stated that it will not change its World Cup preparations despite a warning from the **United States** to isolate for 21 days before arriving in the country due to Ebola fears.  **Andrew Giuliani**, executive director of the White House Task Force for the World Cup, confirmed this requirement. The team is scheduled to play their first group stage match against Portugal on June 17th in Houston, and will be based there throughout the tournament. Despite the health concerns, **the DRC** has maintained its training schedule and no players are currently from the country.
